# SOC-C15 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study (verified on the title page and back cover): McCracken, K., Priest, S., FitzSimons, A., Bracewell, K., Torchia, K., and Parry, W. (Opcit Research), with Stanley, N. (University of Central Lancashire) (2017). Evaluation of Pause. Research report, July 2017. Children's Social Care Innovation Programme Evaluation Report 49. Department for Education, DFE-RR595.

Differences from the reference supplied: Nicky Stanley is listed as "with", after the six Opcit authors; the title page prints "University of Central Lancaster" (typo for Lancashire); report number 49, DFE-RR595.

Text: supplied PDF (85 pages), converted with pdftotext -layout to _text/full.txt. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers (cover = p.1).

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- Object: Pause, a voluntary 18-month programme for women who have experienced repeat removals of children, delivered by a dedicated Practitioner, and working with partner agencies at operational and strategic levels (p.6).
- Relationships studied: Practitioner and woman (trust, emotional, practical and behavioural support, p.45-52); Pause and partner agencies (direct advocacy, Pause Boards, adjustment of access protocols, p.42-45); women and social care (p.29-30).
- Public funding: funded by the Department for Education Innovation Programme in 2015 to expand to seven local authority Practices (p.6); Practices in Hackney, Doncaster, Greenwich, Hull, Islington, Newham, Southwark; partners include children's social care, NHS, housing, probation (p.43-44).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: two Poisson count models of pregnancies avoided (125 Pause women, 134 comparison women; Table 13 p.33, Appendix C p.66-72); longitudinal analysis of 326 Client Monitoring Forms from 115 women (Tables 14-18, p.36-41); fiscal cost benefit analysis (Tables 19-20, p.56-57).
- Qualitative: semi-structured interviews with 105 women, 39 Pause professionals and 34 partner professionals at up to 3 time-points, 4 focus groups, 14 case studies, observation of Boards and group sessions (p.7, p.16-17); thematic findings p.26-31 and p.42-54.

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.
